claims.claim_text: The first of two consecutive Ernest D Clark index rows has a confirmed match to the exact name and private identifier in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private identifier selects one exact-name row among eight Ernest D Clark Army records and dates Army entry to 10 July 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier and exact indexed name are decisive; the second index row carries a different identifier and remains separate.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry but does not date OSS service or prove the occupational category was immediately prior.
claims.match_notes: The selected row's malformed grade field is preserved and not corrected. No facts are transferred from the second Ernest D Clark record.

claims.claim_text: The selected Army row's standard occupation position records Engineers, stationary, subject to a record-quality warning.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-matched Army row carries occupation value 772, which the visually inspected NARA code page labels Engineers, stationary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact indexed name and private identifier establish that the selected row belongs to this first Ernest D Clark index record.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed with an Army entry date of 10 July 1942; work dates and relation to OSS entry remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: The public qualification identifies the malformed grade field. No employer, plant, engineering specialty, military grade or work period is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The second consecutive Ernest D Clark index row supplies a private identifier that selects an Army record with middle initial K; the records remain unmerged.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed identifier selects an exact-last-and-first-name Army row whose middle initial differs from the printed OSS index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: A direct middle-initial disagreement attached to the same private identifier requires conflict status pending review of the original records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The candidate Army row predates the end of OSS, but no candidate occupation, location, grade or assignment is transferred while identity conflicts.
claims.match_notes: The row remains separate from both the first Ernest D Clark index record and the Army record unless Box 126 reconciles the discrepancy.

claims.claim_text: One exact-name Francis V Clark Army entry remains a private identity candidate.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The complete Army file contains one exact-name row, but the OSS index supplies no private identifier, rank, hometown or unit to bridge it.
claims.identity_match_assessment: An exact common name and middle initial are relevant but insufficient without at least two corroborating identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The candidate Army entry predates the end of OSS but does not establish identity, employment or an OSS pathway.
claims.match_notes: Retained for Box 126 comparison; excluded from public facts and analytics.

claims.claim_text: Frederick L Clark has a high-confidence match to an exact-name, exact-private-identifier record in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private identifier selects one exact-name row among eight Frederick L Clark Army records and carries an 11 May 1939 entry date.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name and private identifier are exceptionally specific, but internal anomalies in other selected-row fields keep the assessment below confirmed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The record establishes a dated Army-file observation but not the route or date of later OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Blank grade and branch fields and anomalous birth-year data are not interpreted; no personnel category is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The selected Army row's standard occupation position records Furniture manufacturing occupations, n.e.c., subject to a record-quality warning.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-matched row carries occupation value 636, which the visually inspected NARA code page labels Furniture manufacturing occupations, n.e.c.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact indexed name and private identifier provide a high-confidence identity match despite anomalies in other row fields.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed with an Army-file entry date of 11 May 1939; work dates and relation to OSS entry remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: The public qualification identifies the row anomalies. No employer, product, plant, specialty, military category or work period is inferred.

claims.claim_text: George H Clark has a confirmed match to the exact name and private identifier in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private identifier selects one exact-name record among forty-two George H Clark Army rows and dates Army entry to 9 March 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier and exact indexed name are decisive among numerous common-name candidates.
claims.temporal_assessment: The record dates Army entry but does not date OSS service or prove the occupational category was immediately prior.
claims.match_notes: No employer, design specialty or immediate OSS predecessor is inferred.

claims.claim_text: An official Army-entry record assigns George H Clark the broad occupational category Designers; no employer or design specialty is identified.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-matched Army row carries occupation value 046, decoded on the visually inspected official NARA code page.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier selects the indexed person from forty-two exact-name Army candidates.
claims.temporal_assessment: The code was captured at Army entry on 9 March 1942; whether it was his immediate pre-OSS work is unknown.
claims.match_notes: Occupation remains distinct from employer and self-employment; no organization, design field or workplace is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Two exact-name-with-suffix George O Clark Jr. Army entries remain separate private identity candidates.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The complete Army file contains two exact-name-with-suffix rows, but the index supplies no private identifier, rank, hometown or unit to distinguish them.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Name and suffix alone are insufficient for this common surname; neither candidate has two corroborating identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both candidate Army entries predate the end of OSS but establish no identity, employment or OSS pathway.
claims.match_notes: Both candidates remain separate and are excluded from public facts and analytics pending Box 126 review.

claims.claim_text: Ellery Harding Clark Jr., a documented World War II naval officer, is a rejected private lead for indexed Ellery D Clark.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The SABR biography documents Harvard graduation, a 1933 naval commission and World War II Navy service for Ellery Harding Clark Jr.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare first and last names invite review, but the middle initial conflicts and no indexed identifier or OSS evidence bridges the candidate.
claims.temporal_assessment: The candidate's Navy service spans the relevant era, but no source establishes any OSS assignment or pre-OSS sequence for the indexed person.
claims.match_notes: The candidate is retained only for archival comparison and is excluded from public facts and analytics.
